title: Best AI Checkers Similar to Turnitin: 9 Independently Ranked Picks
summary: You cannot buy Turnitin. Compare 9 AI and plagiarism checkers ranked on independent evidence, not vendor accuracy claims.
body_text: You cannot buy Turnitin. There is no individual plan, no free student sign-up, no way to run your own essay through the exact tool your school uses before you submit it. Access comes only through an institution’s paid license. So when you want to self-check your writing, which tool actually behaves like Turnitin, and can you trust a “best” list written by a company selling its own detector? Every page-one result for the best AI checkers similar to Turnitin is a vendor blog ranking its own product first, usually with an unsourced accuracy claim between 95% and 99.98%. We sell none of these tools. I ranked these 9 Turnitin alternatives on independent evidence: official pricing, peer-reviewed studies, and real user sentiment, not marketing numbers. Below, you get the AI-and-plagiarism combo judged the way Turnitin works, each pick labeled for students, researchers, or institutions , honest accuracy caveats, and why no tool fully matches Turnitin. What Makes a Real Turnitin Alternative (and Why Nothing Fully Matches It) Turnitin is institution-only. Individuals cannot license it at any price. Institutions pay wildly different rates for it, too: CUNY’s 200,000-student system paid $1.79 per student , while UC Irvine’s continuing-education division paid over $6.50 (The Markup, 2025). That single access barrier is the reason this whole category exists. Here is the part no competitor list will tell you. Turnitin’s real advantage is not its AI detector. It is a private database of hundreds of millions of previously submitted student papers, built over decades, that no public tool can check against. Any self-serve alternative can match Turnitin on web and journal plagiarism, and several match it on AI detection. None can replicate that student-paper archive. So “similar to Turnitin” is structurally partial. Set your expectations there. How Turnitin’s AI Detector Actually Works Here is how Turnitin’s AI detector works, so you can judge the alternatives: It uses perplexity and burstiness statistics (how predictable and how varied your sentences are). It splits your text into roughly 5-to-10-sentence segments and scores each one. It only visually flags a segment near 98% confidence , and needs a 300-word minimum to score at all. Blue highlighting means “AI-generated”; purple means “AI-generated, then paraphrased.” Purple exists largely because of paraphrasers like QuillBot (pick 8). The Ranking Criteria I ranked the nine tools below against the criteria that actually decide the purchase: Genuine AI-and-plagiarism combo , like Turnitin. AI-only or gated-plagiarism tools are flagged as partial replacements. Real accessibility or a free tier for students who cannot buy Turnitin. Accuracy backed by independent evidence , never a vendor’s own accuracy claim. Privacy and data handling : does the tool store your unpublished paper? LMS integration (Canvas, Moodle, Blackboard) for the educator and institution audience. Transparent, current pricing with the real free-tier caps spelled out. Even Turnitin’s own AI detector is unreliable enough that at least a dozen universities switched it off . Full evidence in the closing section, not here. 1. GPTZero: Best Free AI Checker for Students This is the one tool here you can start using free today, up to about 10,000 words a month , no payment, no trial clock. That is the most generous ongoing free tier of any major standalone detector, and my first pick for students who need a free AI checker but cannot access Turnitin. Pricing: Free (~10,000 words/mo); Essential ~$14.99/mo, or $8.33/mo billed annually (150,000 words); Premium ~$23.99/mo, or $12.99/mo billed annually (300,000 words, adds plagiarism check and citation sourcing). Best for: Students and individual writers self-checking on a budget. The AI-and-plagiarism combo only arrives on the paid Premium tier, so the free plan is AI-detection only, a partial replacement. Key Features ~10,000 words/month of free AI detection Plagiarism check plus citation sourcing on Premium Chrome extension and standalone web tool Built by an educator (founder Edward Tian, then a Princeton senior) Markets FERPA/GDPR compliance with SOC2 Type-II certification Pros ✔️ Most generous free tier of any major detector, enough to check a full essay without paying ✔️ Built for educators and widely used in that market ✔️ Strong on raw, unedited AI text , catching 10/10 samples in one independent 50-sample test ✔️ Solid marketed compliance certifications for institutions Cons ❌ Lowest user rating of the group at 2.3/5 on Trustpilot (135 reviews), with recurring “flagged my human writing as AI” complaints, including fully human work scored 100% AI ❌ Highest false-positive rate of the five tools in that independent test (12% on human writing) ❌ No native LMS plugin , unlike Copyleaks or Turnitin ❌ Vulnerable to paraphrasing , since it leans on perplexity signals Best for a fast, free gut-check before you submit. Skip it if you need one subscription covering both AI and plagiarism, or if you write in non-native English and worry a strict free tool will overstate your risk. Because GPTZero errs strict, your self-check number may read higher than your school’s actual Turnitin scan . 2. Originality.ai: Best Accuracy for Researchers and Serious Writers In an independent 50-sample test of five detectors, Originality.ai posted the single highest overall accuracy at 74% . Read that again: the best tool tested still missed roughly a quarter of the time , and none cracked 80%. “Best in class” here does not mean “reliable enough to accuse anyone,” a point I come back to in the closing section. Pricing: No ongoing free plan. Pro $12.95/mo billed annually ($14.95 monthly, 2,000 credits/mo); Enterprise $136.58/mo annually ($179 monthly, 15,000 credits/mo). One credit covers 100 words. AI-only scans cost 1 credit per 100 words; combined AI-and-plagiarism scans cost 2. Purchased credits expire after 2 years, plan credits monthly. Best for: Researchers, agencies, publishers, and paid writers who need defensible accuracy and true combined scans. Key Features Highest independent accuracy in the cited 50-sample test Combined AI and plagiarism scanning in one pass Resists paraphrasing and humanizer evasion better than perplexity-only tools Bundles grammar, readability, a fact-check aid, and an SEO optimizer Pros ✔️ Top independent accuracy (74%) of the five detectors tested ✔️ Highest user rating of the standalone detectors, 4.6/5 on Trustpilot (~1,000 reviews), plus ~4.4 on G2 ✔️ Resists evasion tools better than most, since it does not rely on perplexity alone ✔️ Broad feature bundle beyond detection Cons ❌ No free plan at all , a real barrier for students ❌ Credit pricing adds up when you re-check full papers, since combined scans burn 2 credits per 100 words ❌ Credits expire , so unused capacity does not roll over forever ❌ Self-published “RAID #1” claim directly conflicts with GPTZero’s own “RAID #1” claim, proof that vendor benchmark boasts, this one included, deserve skepticism Verdict: Originality.ai is the accuracy leader on paper and the right call for people who can pay per scan. It is the wrong call for a student who simply needs free access. 3. Copyleaks: Best for Educators and Institutions Most standalone detectors leave educators copy-pasting essays one at a time into a web box. Copyleaks plugs straight into the learning management system instead , as an LTI plugin across seven platforms: Canvas, Moodle, D2L Brightspace, Schoology, Sakai, Edsby, and Blackboard, plus an API. That is the broadest LMS reach of any tool here , and it is why departments pick it. Pricing: Free (~25,000 characters, roughly 1,200 words/mo); paid from $13.99/mo billed annually ($16.99 monthly), about $1.40 per 10,000 words on the Personal plan. Best for: Educators and institutions that want LMS-embedded AI-and-plagiarism scanning, and API buyers. Key Features Seven-platform LMS integration plus API access Combined AI and plagiarism detection Markets “FERPA Ready” status , no PII retention, SOC2/SOC3, and GDPR compliance Best-of-five on humanized text in the independent 50-sample test Pros ✔️ Broadest LMS integration of any tool in this guide ✔️ Strongest institutional compliance posture on paper ✔️ Best independent result on humanized text , catching 4/10 where rivals caught fewer Cons ❌ Low user rating , 2.4/5 on Trustpilot (332 reviews) ❌ Misclassifies roughly 1 in 20 human documents as AI in one comparison, too high to base an accusation on ❌ Thin free tier at about 1,200 words ❌ Stores your documents by default : Copyleaks indexes submissions into its internal database and reuses them to catch your own later self-plagiarism, so a checked draft can flag your revised final unless you opt each document out of indexing That last point deserves real weight. If you check a draft, then submit a polished version to the same tool later, your own earlier upload can trip a self-plagiarism match. Best for a department standardizing on one LMS-integrated tool. Skip it if you are an individual who will never touch the LMS features, or if you need a large free allowance. 4. Winston AI: Best for Detecting AI Images and Deepfakes Too Winston AI is the only pick here that also tells you whether an image or video is AI-generated or a deepfake , not just text. It also carries the boldest accuracy claim in the whole category. So how much of that “99.98%” is real, and how much is marketing? Pricing: Free plan (2,000 credits, roughly a 14-day trial) with a claimed 80,000 words/mo of AI detection; Essential $10 to $18/mo; Advanced $16 to $29/mo (200,000 credits, adds advanced plagiarism and HUMN-1 certification, up to 5 seats); Elite $26 to $49/mo (500,000 credits, unlimited seats). AI detection costs 1 credit/word, plagiarism 2 credits/word. Best for: Publishers, content teams, and educators who also need AI-image or deepfake detection and human-content certification. Key Features AI text, image, and deepfake detection in one tool HUMN-1 human-content certification badge for publishers Large claimed free word allowance ~4.4/5 on G2 Pros ✔️ Unique AI-image and deepfake detection no other tool here offers ✔️ Large free-word allowance for casual checking ✔️ HUMN-1 certification useful for publishers signaling human authorship ✔️ Some reviewers cite accuracy positively Cons ❌ That “99.98% accuracy” claim has no independent study behind it ; treat it as a marketing number, not a fact ❌ False-positive complaints on Reddit and review sites, especially on edited human text ❌ Pricing reported inconsistently across sources ($10 to $18 vs $16 to $29), so verify at checkout ❌ Combo requires the Advanced tier , so the cheapest paid plan is a partial replacement I recommend Winston AI specifically for mixed-media checking , when you need text plus image or deepfake detection in one place. For text-only accuracy, picks 1 through 3 have stronger independent evidence behind them. 5. Scribbr: Best Academic Plagiarism Checker for a One-Off Paper Scribbr gives you a free AI detector you can run right now, no account , unlimited scans up to 1,200 words each. Pair that with a plagiarism checker students say rivals what universities use, and it becomes the pick for one big paper rather than a monthly habit . Pricing: The plagiarism checker is pay-per-document, not a subscription: $19.95 (under 7,500 words), $29.95 (under 50,000), $39.95 (longer). The free AI detector runs unlimited scans at 1,200 words each with no account. Premium AI detection covering GPT-4o, Claude, and Gemini is bundled with paid plans from around $17.95. Best for: Students and researchers checking one long paper or thesis for plagiarism without committing to a subscription. Key Features Pay-per-document plagiarism checking , no ongoing fee Free, no-account AI detector Self-plagiarism add-on to check against your own prior documents Immediate data deletion after you receive the report Pros ✔️ Academically credible plagiarism database , per Scribbr’s own positioning ✔️ Genuinely free AI detector with no signup wall ✔️ Privacy win : you can delete all your personal data and uploads from Scribbr’s servers as soon as your report lands ✔️ Self-plagiarism add-on for reusing your own earlier work safely Cons ❌ Free AI detector only catches older models (GPT-2, GPT-3, GPT-3.5), so it will miss GPT-4o, Claude, and Gemini output unless you upgrade (~$17.95+) ❌ Pay-per-document adds up across multiple drafts ❌ Two separate pricing systems make total cost harder to compare Verdict: Scribbr is the best-value plagiarism check for a single important document . Just do not lean on its free AI detector to catch modern AI writing, because it was built for a previous generation of models. 6. Quetext: Best Pay-For-What-You-Need Pricing Tired of paying for an AI detector when you only wanted a plagiarism check, or the reverse? Quetext is the rare tool that sells each capability on its own , so you never buy a bundle you will not use. Pricing: Free (1,000 words each for plagiarism and AI detection); Essential $19.99/mo (100,000 words, all features); standalone Plagiarism-Only $9.99/mo (50,000 words); standalone AI-Only $7.99/mo (50,000 words, line-by-line); Professional from $29.98/mo, scaling up to 14.9 million words/mo. Best for: Budget users who need just one capability, and high-volume users who want granular scaling without an opaque “contact sales” tier. Key Features Standalone plagiarism-only and AI-only plans Free tier that covers both tools Line-by-line AI analysis Scales to millions of words a month Pros ✔️ Cheapest way to buy a single capability at $7.99 to $9.99/mo ✔️ Free tier includes both tools , not just one ✔️ Transparent high-volume scaling with no forced sales call Cons ❌ Bundled Essential costs more ($19.99) than buying GPTZero or Copyleaks alone at similar volume ❌ 1,000-word free cap is among the smallest here ❌ Also sells an AI humanizer , the same evasion conflict of interest I flag on QuillBot; self-checking is fine, disguising AI writing is not (more in the closing section) Best for anyone who needs exactly one tool cheaply. Skip it if you want the combined AI-and-plagiarism scan, where the bundled tier is simply overpriced against the competition. 7. Paperpal: Best for Graduate Students and Researchers Paperpal’s plagiarism check runs against 99 billion webpages plus 200 million Open Access research articles . That research-oriented corpus is exactly what a thesis or journal submission needs, and it is the kind of source pool general web checkers skip. Pricing: Free plagiarism up to 7,000 words/mo (~25 pages); free AI detector at 5 scans/day, 1,200 words each. Prime is $25/mo ($55/quarter, $139/yr) and raises plagiarism to 10,000 words/mo with color-coded, side-by-side reports; extra word blocks are purchasable. Best for: Graduate students and researchers checking academic writing against scholarly sources. Key Features Academic plagiarism database with 200 million Open Access articles Combined AI detection, plagiarism, and academic writing support (grammar, style, citations) Relatively generous 7,000-word free plagiarism allowance Pros ✔️ Research-specific database relevant to theses and papers ✔️ All-in-one academic writing platform , not just a detector ✔️ Generous free plagiarism cap compared with most peers Cons ❌ Thin free AI detector (1,200 words per scan, 5 a day), weak for a full chapter ❌ Prime is pricey at $25/mo, above pure detectors, yet still caps plagiarism at 10,000 words/mo ❌ Detector-accuracy data is thinner than GPTZero, Copyleaks, or Originality, since Paperpal is built as a broad writing assistant I recommend Paperpal specifically for researchers who value the academic source database . If you mainly want detector accuracy, picks 1 through 3 give you more independent evidence to stand on. 8. QuillBot: Best All-in-One Bundle for the Price Here is the strangest entry on this list: a tool that will both detect AI writing and paraphrase text to disguise it . Turnitin’s purple “AI-paraphrased” highlight essentially exists because of tools like this one. That contradiction is real, and I will not pretend otherwise, but the bundle is genuinely cheap . Pricing: Free (125-word paraphrase cap, 125-word humanizer at 6 uses/day, limited plagiarism, 20 AI chats); Premium $8.33/mo billed annually (unlimited paraphrasing and humanizing, 25,000 words/mo plagiarism, unlimited AI chat). Best for: Budget users who want paraphrasing, summarizing, plagiarism, and AI detection in one cheap subscription, for legitimate self-checking only. Key Features Broadest feature bundle per dollar at $8.33/mo 25,000 words/mo of plagiarism checking on Premium AI detection plus paraphrase, summarize, and humanizer tools Free tier for basic testing Pros ✔️ Cheapest broad bundle of any tool here ✔️ Caught real plagiarism that Grammarly missed, flagging 46% and 91.2% matches in independent testing ✔️ Genuinely useful for drafting , not only checking Cons ❌ Direct conflict of interest : its own humanizer defeats its own detector, and universities treat humanizer-based evasion as misconduct ❌ Indexes mostly free web sources , so it under-detects paywalled academic plagiarism ❌ AI detection is a secondary feature , less independently scrutinized than dedicated detectors Verdict: QuillBot is great value for legitimate self-checking and drafting. Use the detector, ignore the humanizer , and do not expect academic-database depth on plagiarism. 9. Grammarly: Best If You Already Use It If Grammarly already lives in your browser, you can run an AI or plagiarism check without adopting a single new tool . And its Authorship view does something none of the others attempt: instead of a black-box probability score, it categorizes each passage by how it was made . Pricing: Free (10 AI-detection scans/mo, up to 1,500 words each); Premium $12/mo billed annually ($30 monthly) for unlimited AI scans plus plagiarism; student discount brings it to about $7.50/mo annualized; Business from $15/member/mo. Best for: Existing Grammarly users who want a no-new-tool check, and writers who prefer a process view over a probability score. Key Features Authorship categorizes each passage by origin: typed by you, AI-generated, pasted from a database, or grammar-edited Plagiarism checking against billions of web pages Unlimited AI scans on Premium Already installed for most students Pros ✔️ Honest, transparent Authorship approach instead of a single opaque score ✔️ Zero adoption friction if you already use it ✔️ Cheap with the student discount Cons ❌ Missed plagiarism in independent testing : Grammarly reported “no plagiarism found” on a document where QuillBot found 46% and Turnitin found 64% ❌ Inconsistent results : it flagged a 100%-copied article on one scan, then missed it on a rescan of the same text ❌ Free scan cap (10/mo) is too thin for regular academic use, and the database is not academic-specific Best for a convenience check you already own. Skip it as your primary plagiarism defense, because those misses in testing make it the weakest combo pick on this list . AI Checkers Compared: Pricing, Free Tiers, and Accuracy at a Glance Everything you need to choose sits in one table, so you do not have to scroll back through nine sections. Read it by starting with your audience column , then check whether the free tier actually covers your word count and whether you need the full AI-and-plagiarism checker or just one half. Tool Best for AI + plagiarism combo Free tier Starting price Independent accuracy / sentiment LMS integration Turnitin (baseline) Institutions Yes (native) None (institution-only) Quote-only, ~$1.79 to $6.50/student 72% in 50-sample test; tuned to under-flag Native (Canvas, Blackboard, Moodle) GPTZero Students Premium only ~10,000 words/mo Free; paid ~$8.33/mo annual 2.3 Trustpilot; 12% false positives None (Chrome extension) Originality.ai Researchers Yes None $12.95/mo annual 74% (highest tested); 4.6 Trustpilot None Copyleaks Educators Yes ~1,200 words/mo $13.99/mo annual 2.4 Trustpilot; best on humanized text 7 platforms + API Winston AI Mixed media Advanced tier only ~80,000-word claim/trial $10 to $18/mo ~4.4 G2; “99.98%” is an unverified claim Limited Scribbr One-off papers Weak (old models free) Free AI, 1,200/scan $19.95/document Academically credible plagiarism DB None Quetext Single capability Optional (modular) 1,000 words each $7.99 to $9.99/mo standalone Line-by-line analysis None Paperpal Grad researchers Yes 7,000 words plagiarism $25/mo Research-oriented database None QuillBot Budget bundle Yes 125-word cap $8.33/mo annual Caught matches Grammarly missed None Grammarly Existing users Yes (inconsistent) 10 scans/mo $12/mo annual Missed matches in testing None There is no single winner. The right pick depends on which constraint binds hardest for you: free access (GPTZero, Scribbr, Paperpal), defensible accuracy (Originality.ai), or LMS integration (Copyleaks). Turnitin sits at the top only as the baseline you are trying to approximate, not as an option you can buy. Every accuracy and rating figure above comes from independent sources (the 50-sample test, Trustpilot, G2), not vendor marketing, and each varies by sample and text type. I unpack exactly how unreliable these numbers get next. No AI Detector Is Proof: The Accuracy Evidence and What to Do If You’re Wrongly Flagged In Temple University’s controlled 120-text study, Turnitin’s sentence-level AI flags had “no relationship at all” to which sentences were actually AI-written, and it was technically correct on only 43% of realistic hybrid papers . The most-trusted detector in education fails hardest on the fastest-growing kind of student writing. The Evidence Every Vendor List Only Name-Drops Temple University (120 texts): 93% correct on pure human writing, but 63% on paraphrased AI . Turnitin is tuned to favor human writers, so it under-flags rather than over-accuses. Stanford / Liang et al. (Patterns, 2023): more than half of non-native-English TOEFL essays were wrongly flagged as AI. Author James Zou warned of significant consequences for admissions and coursework. RAID benchmark (ACL 2024, 6M+ generations): detectors are “easily fooled” by paraphrasing and unseen models. GPTZero and Originality both claim “#1” on it, so trust the paper, not vendor summaries . Washington Post testing: found false positives, one small-sample analysis hitting 50% . A Turnitin VP admitted the tool flags writing “too consistently average.” Independent 50-sample test: no detector exceeded 80% accuracy , and 45% of human samples scored above 20% AI on at least one tool. Turnitin’s own caveat: its “under 1% false positives” claim applies only to documents already 20%+ AI-flagged . On lower-scored documents, its AI detection accuracy is far weaker. Why Schools Quit Vanderbilt disabled the detector in 2023 : its ~75,000 annual submissions could wrongly flag about 750 students a year . Waterloo found human text scored 100% AI, and a dozen elite schools from Yale to MIT followed. All kept plagiarism checking and dropped only AI detection. What to Do If You Are Wrongly Flagged Keep your drafts and version history. The Johns Hopkins false-positive case was resolved exactly this way. Keep any permitted AI-interaction transcript to prove you followed your syllabus. Insist the score is one input, not proof. GDPR Article 22 bars sole-automated academic decisions without human review. Cite the bias literature if your writing is non-native English, heavily edited, or AI-assisted. Run two or three tools, not one. Aggregating them pushes false-positive risk toward zero. Self-checking your own original work is legitimate. Using a humanizer to disguise AI writing is misconduct under university integrity policies, so I recommend no humanizer here, even though a page-one competitor sells one. Frequently Asked Questions Is there a free version of Turnitin for students? No. Turnitin has no individual or public plan; access comes only through an institution’s paid license. To self-check, use standalone tools like GPTZero’s free tier, Scribbr’s free AI detector, or Quetext’s free tier. GPTZero’s is the most generous at roughly 10,000 words a month. Just know that none is calibrated identically to Turnitin, so your number will not match your school’s scan. Which AI detector is most similar to Turnitin? There is no consensus, and most “closest to Turnitin” claims come from vendors ranking themselves. Independent testing suggests Originality.ai and GPTZero track closest on raw AI text , since both use similar perplexity signals. But no tool matches Turnitin’s private student-paper database , and the rankings flip depending on text type. Any AI detector like Turnitin is only a partial match. Is it cheating to run my own paper through an AI checker before I submit? Research surfaced no university policy that prohibits self-checking your own original work . The integrity line is about generating work with AI or using tools to evade detection, not verifying writing you wrote yourself. Policies still vary, so check your specific syllabus before you rely on this. Are AI humanizer tools that bypass Turnitin considered cheating? Generally yes. University integrity guidance treats deliberately disguising AI-generated content to evade detection as misconduct, because it misrepresents AI work as your own, regardless of whether a detector catches it. That is why I do not recommend any humanizer in this guide, even ones sold alongside detectors by tools on this list. Can a free checker store my paper or flag me for self-plagiarism later? It depends on the tool. Copyleaks indexes submissions into its internal database by default and can flag your own revised version later, unless you opt out per document. Scribbr, by contrast, lets you delete your data right after the report. Check each vendor’s policy before you upload unpublished work. How accurate is Turnitin’s AI detection, really? Turnitin claims under 1% false positives, but only for documents already 20%+ AI-flagged . Independently, the picture is rougher: Temple University found 93% accuracy on human text but 43% on hybrid text , a 50-sample test put it at 72%, and Washington Post testing hit a 50% false-positive rate in a small sample. Treat any score as an indicator, not proof.

title: DAVID GOLDSEN ELEVATED TO EVP, A&R FOR WARNER CHAPPELL MUSIC
summary: Key figure behind culture-shifting songwriters such as Zach Bryan, Sleep Token, Mitski,. . .
body_text: Key figure behind culture-shifting songwriters such as Zach Bryan, Sleep Token, Mitski, and the Red Clay Strays Warner Chappell Music (WCM) today announced the promotion of David Goldsen to Executive Vice President, A&R. Since joining the publisher in 2009, Goldsen has discovered and championed a diverse range of chart-topping songwriters, further expanding WCM’s creative presence across both North America and Australia. Based at the company’s Los Angeles headquarters, he will continue to report to Ryan Press, President, North America, WCM. Over the course of his 17-year career at WCM, Goldsen has worked closely with some of today’s most culturally significant songwriting talent, ranging from the meteoric success of Zach Bryan and Sleep Token to the breakout of Teddy Swims. He has also played a pivotal role in the development of acclaimed artists such as Mitski, Vance Joy, the Red Clay Strays, and Tones and I. Goldsen has maintained a steadfast focus on creating a songwriter-first environment while expanding international opportunities and unlocking new creative avenues. His accomplishments were recognized in 2024, when he was named to Billboard’s prestigious 40 Under 40 list. Ryan Press commented: “I’ve had the pleasure of working with David for over 15 years. He has a rare ability to spot talent ahead of what’s hot before it breaks mainstream, and to guide them toward not just their personal dreams, but real cultural impact. Watching him turn that instinct into massive wins for our songwriters and our team has been incredibly rewarding. He’s become a key leader in Warner Chappell’s continued evolution.” David Goldsen said: “I’ve been extremely lucky to work with many of the best songwriters in music. Thank you to Ryan for being a mentor and for trusting me all this time, and to Guy, Carianne, and the entire WCM team who have always put songwriters first. I’m forever grateful to all of them for continuing to support me and allowing our global team to champion great songwriting, bring our ideas to life, and follow our passions to create the best home for creatives.” Goldsen’s promotion comes amid a wave of powerful momentum for the publisher. WCM’s genre-diverse roster continues to move culture and lead the global charts, anchored by Amy Allen’s consecutive Songwriter of the Year Grammy wins. Among the company’s recent achievements, WCM hitmakers MAG and Scott Dittrich made history this year with Bad Bunny’s record-breaking global Latin anthem, “DtMF,” while the publisher has also scored chart-topping releases by Cardi B, Don Toliver, and ROSÉ, among others.

title: SunCoke Energy, Inc. Announces First Quarter 2026 Earnings Date
summary: LISLE, Ill.--(BUSINESS WIRE)-- SunCoke Energy, Inc. (NYSE: SXC) plans to release its first quarter 2026 financial results on Thursday, April 30, 2026, before trading opens on the New York Stock Exchange. SXC will host its quarterly earnings call at 11:00 am ET on April 30, 2026. The conference call will be webcast live
body_text: Press Releases 2026 Home Investors Press Releases SunCoke Energy, Inc. Announces First Quarter 2026 Earnings Date LISLE, Ill.--(BUSINESS WIRE)-- SunCoke Energy, Inc. (NYSE: SXC) plans to release its first quarter 2026 financial results on Thursday, April 30, 2026, before trading opens on the New York Stock Exchange. SXC will host its quarterly earnings call at 11:00 am ET on April 30, 2026. The conference call will be webcast live at https://event.choruscall.com/mediaframe/webcast.html?webcastid=RDZPXkjz and archived for replay in the Investors section of www.suncoke.com . Investors and analysts may participate in this call by dialing 1-833-821-7847 in the U.S. or 1-412-652-1261 if outside the U.S., and asking to be joined into the SunCoke Energy, Inc. call. ABOUT SUNCOKE ENERGY, INC. SunCoke Energy, Inc. (NYSE: SXC) supplies high-quality coke to domestic and international customers. Our coke is used in the blast furnace production of steel as well as the foundry production of casted iron, with the majority of sales under long-term, take-or-pay contracts. We also export coke to overseas customers seeking high-quality product for their blast furnaces. Our process utilizes an innovative heat-recovery technology that captures excess heat for steam or electrical power generation and draws upon more than 60 years of cokemaking experience to operate our facilities in Illinois, Indiana, Ohio, Virginia and Brazil. Our industrial services business provides export and domestic material handling services to coke, coal, steel, power and other bulk customers, as well as mission-critical services to leading steel producers globally. The logistics terminals have the collective capacity to mix and transload more than 40 million tons of material each year and are strategically located to reach Gulf Coast, East Coast, Great Lakes and international ports. Additional industrial services include the removal, handling, and processing of molten slag at customer sites, as well as preparation and transportation of metal scraps, raw materials, and finished products. To learn more about SunCoke Energy, Inc., visit our website at www.suncoke.com . title: How AI Is Reinventing Retail Replenishment
summary: Fixed reorder rules break down at scale. See how AI-driven replenishment adapts to real demand signals, lead times, and network conditions daily.
body_text: By Elie Dufeu, CTO & Co-Founder, Metreecs. Published July 2026. AI-driven replenishment replaces fixed reorder rules with daily, product-level demand signals, so restocking decisions reflect what is actually selling right now instead of a static minimum set months ago. The result is fewer stockouts and less excess inventory sitting in the wrong location. Retailers have run replenishment the same way for decades: set a minimum stock level per product, reorder when inventory drops below it, repeat. That rule holds up fine when demand is flat. It breaks the moment demand isn't, which for most retail categories is most of the time. Marcus, a demand planner at a 25-store home goods chain, saw this play out last March. A bestselling product ran out in three stores over one weekend, and the first sign anyone had of it was Monday's report, two full days after the shelves went empty and the sales had already been lost. Key Takeaways Retailers using AI-driven inventory systems report stockout reductions in the 26-32% range across recent industry studies (Prophet+LightGBM grocery deployment, various platform benchmarks). McKinsey finds companies applying AI to procurement and inventory see a 35-65% improvement in inventory and service levels, alongside a 15% reduction in logistics costs. Gartner reports that AI-driven replenishment systems can cut excess inventory by up to 50% while improving service levels. Fixed reorder points fail because they assume stable demand, but seasonality, promotions, and local variation make that assumption wrong most of the time. NRF's 2026 retail trends report puts inventory and demand forecasting at roughly 23% of retail AI spend, the single largest planned AI use case for 2026. What is AI-driven replenishment? AI-driven replenishment is the use of machine learning models to generate reorder recommendations for each product and variant, updated daily using current sell-through, lead times, and stock position, rather than a fixed minimum stock threshold reviewed on a weekly or monthly cycle. It replaces static rules with a forecast that adjusts as demand changes. That distinction matters more than it sounds. A fixed reorder point is a bet that next month looks like last month. AI-driven replenishment removes the bet: it recalculates the reorder trigger every time new sales data comes in. Curious what daily, product-level reorder recommendations would look like for your own catalog? See Metreecs in action on your product data . See how a replenishment upgrade fits into a broader stockout-and-overstock strategy → Why fixed reorder rules break down at scale A minimum stock level is a single number applied to a product regardless of what's actually happening in the market. That works until one of three things changes, and in most retail categories, at least one of them changes every week. Demand isn't flat. A product selling 8 units a week in January might sell 30 a week in a promotional spike and 2 a week in a slow season. A fixed reorder point calibrated to the January average triggers a stockout in the spike and overstock in the slow season, sometimes both in the same quarter. Lead times aren't fixed either. Supplier delays, shipping disruptions, and seasonal capacity constraints all shift how long it takes for a reorder to actually arrive. A reorder point built on a 30-day lead time assumption is wrong the moment the real lead time moves to 45 days. Local demand doesn't match network averages. A product moving fast in one store and slowly in another needs a different reorder trigger at each location. A single network-wide minimum stock level averages away the exact information a planner needs to act on. None of this means the planners running fixed reorder points did anything wrong. Weekly or monthly review cycles were the right tool when data refreshed weekly. The gap opened up because sell-through data now updates daily and the reorder logic mostly didn't catch up with it. How AI-driven replenishment actually works AI-driven replenishment starts with a demand forecast at the product and location level, not the category level. Each product and variant, at each store or fulfillment point, gets its own forecast, calibrated to its own sales history, seasonality, and promotional calendar. From there, the system compares the forecast against current stock position, known lead times, and minimum order quantities, and generates a reorder recommendation, refreshed as new data comes in rather than on a fixed schedule. Forecast accuracy compounds into fewer emergency orders. Hybrid forecasting approaches that combine multiple modeling techniques have shown forecast error reductions of 20-40% compared to traditional statistical methods , which directly reduces the number of last-minute, high-cost emergency replenishments a team has to place. Daily refresh closes the lag between signal and action. Instead of a planner reviewing a report on Monday for a stock position that changed on Thursday, the recommendation updates the moment new sell-through data lands. Across Metreecs' work with retailers, the recurring pattern behind both stockouts and overstock is a forecast that was accurate but acted on days too late. Gartner's guidance on retail forecasting and replenishment points to the same gap: systems that close the loop between demand signal and reorder action are what separate retailers cutting excess inventory from those still carrying it, per Gartner's Market Guide for Retail Forecasting, Allocation and Replenishment Solutions . Safety stock adjusts by product, not by category rule. A product with high week-to-week demand variance needs more safety stock than a stable, slow-moving item. Applying one safety stock rule to both either overstocks the stable product or leaves the volatile one exposed. AI-driven replenishment sets the safety stock level per product based on its own demand variability. AI agents built for autonomous inventory decisions extend this further, generating and, where trusted, executing replenishment recommendations without waiting for a planner to manually approve every routine reorder. What this looks like for a planning team Elena runs replenishment for a mid-market footwear retailer with around 40 stores. Before moving to daily, product-level replenishment recommendations, her team reviewed stock positions every Monday against a spreadsheet of fixed minimums, and by Wednesday the numbers were already stale. The failure mode was predictable: a running shoe model that spiked after a local marathon sold out in three stores by Tuesday, while the same style sat in excess at two others. Neither problem showed up until the next Monday review, by which point the stockout had already cost sales and the excess stock was closer to markdown territory. Moving replenishment recommendations to a daily cycle didn't change what Elena's team decided, it changed when they saw the problem. The marathon spike showed up as a reorder flag the same day sell-through jumped, not five days later. Where AI-driven replenishment still needs a human AI-driven replenishment removes the manual math, it doesn't remove judgment. New product launches, supplier renegotiations, and one-off promotional events still need a planner's call on top of the model's recommendation. One mistake we repeatedly see is teams treating every AI recommendation as a draft to double-check by hand, which recreates the exact review bottleneck the system was meant to remove. The practical approach is to auto-approve routine, low-risk reorders and route only genuine exceptions, new products, large deviations, supplier changes, to a human. How to know if it's actually working Switching to AI-driven replenishment is only worth doing if the results show up in numbers a planning team already tracks. Three metrics tell the story: Stockout rate on top-velocity products. This is the fastest signal. If daily replenishment recommendations are working, out-of-stock incidents on your highest-selling products should drop within the first full planning cycle, typically 4-8 weeks. Excess inventory on slow movers. Gartner's analysis of retail forecasting and replenishment systems finds that closing the gap between demand signal and reorder action is what lets retailers cut excess inventory by up to 50% while improving service levels , rather than trading one problem for the other. Time planners spend on manual recalculation versus exceptions. If a team is still recalculating reorder points by hand for routine products, the automation isn't doing its job yet. The goal is a planning calendar where routine reorders clear automatically and a planner's attention goes to the products that actually need a judgment call, new launches, supplier disruptions, unusual demand spikes. Track these three metrics before and after the switch, over the same season if possible, since retail demand has enough seasonal variation that a single month of data can be misleading either way. Getting started with AI-driven replenishment Retailers evaluating a move from fixed reorder points don't need to change everything at once. A few steps make the transition manageable: Identify your highest-velocity products. Start with the 10-20% of products driving the most sales volume, since that's where reorder errors cost the most. Check your current lead time assumptions against reality. Pull actual supplier delivery times from the last two quarters and compare them to what your reorder points assume. Separate safety stock by demand variability , not by category, for at least your top products. Pilot a daily reorder review for the pilot product group before rolling out network-wide. Set clear auto-approval thresholds so routine reorders don't require manual sign-off, freeing planner time for genuine exceptions. A closer look at network-wide inventory KPIs is a useful next step once daily replenishment is in place, since the KPIs that matter change once decisions move from weekly to daily. FAQ What's the difference between automated replenishment and AI-driven replenishment? Automated replenishment can still run on fixed rules, just executed automatically instead of manually. AI-driven replenishment goes further: the reorder trigger itself is generated by a demand forecast that updates as conditions change, rather than a static threshold that happens to be applied by software instead of a person. How often should replenishment recommendations update? Daily, for any product where demand or lead time can shift meaningfully within a week. Weekly review cycles were built for a data environment that no longer exists, most retailers now have daily sell-through data available and are leaving it unused if replenishment logic only runs weekly. Does AI replenishment work for products with no sales history? New products need a different approach since there's no historical demand to learn from. Statistical methods based on comparable products (similar category, price point, or launch pattern) generate an initial forecast, which the model corrects as real sell-through data comes in over the first few weeks. This matters most for retailers with high new-product turnover, where a meaningful share of the catalog has no sales history at any given time. What data does a retailer need before starting? At minimum: historical sales by product and location, current stock positions, and supplier lead times. Most retailers already have this in an ERP or point-of-sale system. The harder part isn't gathering the data, it's making sure lead time assumptions reflect current supplier reality rather than a figure set years ago and never revisited. Will AI replenishment replace a planning team? No. It removes the manual recalculation work behind routine reorders so planners spend their time on exceptions, new product decisions, and supplier strategy, the parts of the job that actually require judgment. How much lead time does a retailer need before switching from fixed reorder points? None, in the sense of a hard prerequisite. Retailers can pilot AI-driven replenishment on a subset of high-velocity products while continuing fixed reorder points elsewhere, then expand as results validate the approach. Conclusion Fixed reorder points were built for a slower, more predictable retail environment. Demand doesn't hold still long enough for a static minimum stock level to stay accurate, and the data to do better than that update daily. The move to AI-driven replenishment isn't about adding complexity, it's about matching the reorder logic to the pace at which demand actually changes. Start with your highest-velocity products, check your lead time assumptions, and build a daily review habit before expanding further. title: GRESB Season Is Here. Cambio is Now an Official GRESB Partner

body_text: GRESB season is officially underway with the portal opening on April 1. But for most real estate teams, the work started months ago. That's because GRESB preparation isn't purely an annual exercise. It's a multi-year performance journey; one that demands continuous data management, tenant coordination, and evidence of genuine impact. Ask any GRESB participant what consumes most of their submission window, and the answer is almost always the same: chasing data. It's a challenge that extends well beyond GRESB — according to KPMG's 2024 ESG Organization Survey, nearly 50% of all organizations are still managing their sustainability data manually. For GRESB participants, that translates directly into hundreds of hours spent chasing utility bills, corralling tenant data, and populating spreadsheets — time that could be spent actually driving performance. This is the problem Cambio was built to solve. We’ve been working with our clients to solve this for years. Now, as an official GRESB partner, we're committed to making that solution available to more participants than ever. ‍ Automating Data Collection Cambio automates the most manual tasks in the GRESB submission process — collecting and aggregating landlord data directly into the GRESB asset level spreadsheet. Through automated utility APIs, OCR bill reading, and intelligent meter tagging, the platform ingests data continuously throughout the year, eliminating the need to chase down bills or reconcile spreadsheets at crunch time. Built-in coverage alerts and performance insights tell your team exactly where to focus — no guesswork, no manual combing. ‍ Streamlining Tenant Outreach Landlord data is one challenge. Tenant data is another entirely — and for most GRESB participants, it's the harder one. Cambio's automated outreach workflows eliminate the cycle of chaser emails and manual follow-ups that consume teams every submission season. Tenants can upload or connect their utility data directly through the platform, removing the need for spreadsheet sharing or manual entry. For harder-to-reach tenants, Cambio's AI voice agent conducts outreach by phone, gathering data conversationally and logging it automatically. The result: faster coverage, less effort, and fewer gaps in your submission. ‍ From Data to Performance: Driving Impact Collecting and reporting data is the prerequisite — but it’s not the goal. The teams that lead are not those who treat collection as a checkbox or hit 100% coverage; they're the ones who use that coverage as a foundation for genuine performance improvements. This is where Cambio helps clients differentiate and focus on financial and carbon impact. We wrote about this in depth in February . Cambio identifies high-impact opportunities at the asset level, quantifies projected energy savings and NOI impact, and tracks realized results after implementation — all aligned with GRESB's Technical Building Assessment (RA2) requirements. If you're focused on the performance side of your score, that piece is worth a read. ‍ What Cambio’s GRESB Partnership Means for You Cambio is now an official GRESB partner — not just a platform that supports the submission process, but a recognized part of the GRESB ecosystem. For clients, that means tighter alignment between Cambio and GRESB, and confidence that the outputs feeding your submission meet the standard's expectations today and as it evolves. GRESB's requirements are more rigorous each year — increasing emphasis on data verification, energy performance improvement, and transparency of methodology. Cambio is built to stay ahead of that curve, so your team doesn't have to. ‍ Ready to see how Cambio fits into your 2026 GRESB submission, reach out to info@cambio.ai to book a demo.
